title: Germanisches Nationalmuseum: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works about effort, occupation and the roles made visible through a pose.
introduction:
Hercules draws a bow with his back turned. An older sister carries a child. Between those actions lies a substantial difference in subject and status, but both paintings must make weight and effort intelligible through the body. That practical question is a useful way into this selection from the Germanisches Nationalmuseum.

Other figures are less physically active. A book, a habit, heraldic signs or theatrical costume may establish what kind of person a portrait presents. Those attributes should not be mistaken for complete access to a sitter's character. Across these works, compare what a body does, what its surroundings say about it, and what the image leaves unknown.
visitNote: This guide selects paintings from a museum whose collections also extend far beyond painting. Some works are long-term loans, and current display can change. Consult the museum’s object catalogue and visitor information before planning an individual stop.

books.title: The Practice and Science of Drawing
books.author: Harold Speed
books.note: Speed’s chapters on contour, tone and the arrangement of figures give practical language for comparing Dürer’s close description with Jawlensky’s strongly coloured head and Oppenheimer’s musicians.

works.title: Hercules Fighting the Stymphalian Birds
works.catalogueTitle: Herkules im Kampf mit den Harpyen
works.credit: Hercules kills the Symphalic Bird. WikiArt; Albrecht Dürer. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The drawn bow turns Hercules into a study of opposing forces. His back faces the viewer, yet the rotation of the body makes the direction of the shot legible. Dürer uses the mythological task to test how movement can be understood from an awkward view. The fantastic creatures supply the target; the hero's anatomy supplies the immediate problem.

works.title: Johannes Reuss
works.credit: Lucas Cranach the Elder. Johannes Reuss. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/lucas-cranach-the-elder/johannes-reuss-1503
works.description: An open book brings the sitter's hands into the portrait's account of identity. Red cap and robe connect head and torso, while trees frame the face against a landscape. Cranach does not rely on expression alone to introduce Reuss. Reading, clothing and setting work together as the public terms through which an individual is presented.

works.title: Annunciation
works.credit: Konrad Witz. Annunciation. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The timbered room puts physical limits around the encounter. Low ceiling, walls and heavy folds of cloth give the angel and Mary a shared material setting. Konrad Witz makes the sacred event happen within a space that has to accommodate bodies. Its closeness matters: the room resists becoming an indefinite backdrop behind two symbolic figures.

works.title: Battle of the Amazons
works.credit: Anselm Feuerbach. Battle of the Amazons. Image credit: Anselm Feuerbach. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: A rearing horse carries one part of the struggle above the surrounding bodies. Across the wide field, repeated limbs and opposing movements connect separate encounters. Feuerbach makes conflict readable through an extensive arrangement rather than one decisive blow. The broad format gives the eye time to move between groups, even while their actions resist a stable balance.

works.title: Behind the Scenes
works.credit: Eduard von Grützner. Behind the Scenes. Image credit: Eduard von Grützner. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Away from the stage, costumes continue to announce roles that the wearers are not currently performing. Grützner divides the company into smaller groups of standing and seated figures. Waiting becomes a subject alongside theatrical display. The distinction between a performer and a character grows easier to notice when the apparatus of performance remains visible during a pause.

works.title: Michael Wolgemut
works.credit: © Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen (als Dauerleihgabe im Germanischen Nationalmuseum Nürnberg). Albrecht Dürer, Bildnis Michael Wolgemut, 1516. https://www.sammlung.pinakothek.de/de/artwork/M0xyZ1VLpl CC BY-SA 4.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: The dark cap and plain ground leave the face with little competition. Dürer follows the uneven contours around eyes, cheeks and mouth rather than smoothing age into a generalised emblem of wisdom. The portrait's specificity lies in those differences. It presents an old man as a particular person without requiring an invented psychological explanation for each line.

works.title: Nuremberg's Main Market from the South
works.catalogueTitle: View of the main market in Nuremberg from the south
works.credit: Lorenz Strauch. View of the main market in Nuremberg from the south. Image credit: Lorenz Strauch; Source credit: Photo from a reproduction. Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The enclosing buildings define a civic space, while stalls and small figures divide it into places of activity. Strauch's church façade anchors the view without absorbing the market around it. Architecture becomes legible through use as well as outline. The small scale of the people allows many separate occupations to remain visible within one account of the city.

works.title: Martin Luther as an Augustinian Monk
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Martin Luther as an Augustinian Monk
works.credit: Lucas Cranach the Elder. Portrait of Martin Luther as an Augustinian Monk. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Habit and book establish a religious role before a fuller history of the sitter is supplied. One hand rises near the chest while the other remains associated with the book. Cranach keeps the face particular within those recognisable signs. The portrait records a mode of presentation, not a face in which every later event can already be read.

works.title: Fool with a Needle and Ass's Ears
works.catalogueTitle: Depiction of a Fool with Needle and Ass's Ears
works.credit: Andreas Herneisen. Depiction of a Fool with Needle and Ass's Ears. Image credit: Sailko; Required attribution: I, Sailko. Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The needle brings the hands close to the grinning face, enlarging a small action within the tight frame. Exaggerated ears in the headgear identify the comic role before the gesture is fully understood. Herneisen makes costume and action reinforce one another. The figure is presented as a performance of foolishness, not as an ordinary portrait accidentally caught in an awkward pose.

works.title: Cornelia Adriana Munter and Her Daughter
works.catalogueTitle: Double portrait of Cornelia Adriana Munter (1770-1828) and her daughter Eleonore Louise Hedwig von Bose (1797-1831)
works.credit: Johann Friedrich August Tischbein. Double portrait of Cornelia Adriana Munter (1770-1828) and her daughter Eleonore Louise Hedwig von Bose (1797-1831). Image credit: Daderot. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The child is held within the larger body's space. Pale faces and clothing emerge from the dim setting above the mother's green dress, making their contact easy to follow. Tischbein gives the double portrait its structure through unequal scale and physical proximity. No additional incident is needed to show the practical relation between holding and being held.

works.title: Emperor Maximilian I
works.credit: Albrecht Dürer. Emperor Maximilian I. Image credit: Albrecht Dürer. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The face is only one part of the imperial presentation. Inscription, heraldic signs and rich clothing extend the sitter's identity beyond likeness into public authority. Dürer's arrangement makes that machinery visible. It is useful to separate what the features tell us from what the accompanying signs declare, rather than treating rank as something naturally apparent in a person's appearance.

works.title: Tegernsee Landscape
works.credit: August Macke. Tegernsee Landscape. Image credit: August Macke. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Bright colour patches make trees, buildings and mountains fit together around the open slope. Macke keeps the terrain recognisable without subordinating every colour to naturalistic shade. Blue and yellow accents can establish relations across different objects. The landscape is organised by how these patches meet as much as by the distances that they describe.

works.title: The Rosé Quartet
works.credit: Max Oppenheimer. Rose Quartet. Image credit: Max Oppenheimer. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Arms, bows and instruments overlap so closely that individual actions become part of a larger web. Oppenheimer gives ensemble playing a visible structure without reducing the four musicians to identical movements. Each has a separate task inside the shared performance. Repeated lines connect them, while the bodies and instruments retain the differences required to make a quartet.

works.title: Two Girls
works.credit: Max Pechstein. Two Girls. Image credit: Max Pechstein; Source credit: Ölgemälde. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: One figure's raised arms interrupt the possibility of a symmetrical pair. Pechstein relies on broad outlines and strong colour to hold the bodies against their surroundings. The contrast in posture remains more consequential than fine anatomical description. Sitting close does not make the figures equivalent; their differing gestures give the arrangement its internal movement.

works.title: Head in Black and Green
works.credit: Alexej von Jawlensky. Head in Black and Green. Image credit: Alexej von Jawlensky. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Green, blue, pink and black cease to describe ordinary skin, but the enlarged eyes and long nose preserve a face. Jawlensky tests how much recognition depends on arrangement rather than local colour. The head remains readable through the position and proportion of a few features, even as its surface refuses the conventions of a naturalistic likeness.

works.title: Ideal Landscape with the Temple of Juno at Agrigento
works.catalogueTitle: Ideal Landscape with Juno Temple of Agrigento
works.credit: Jacob Philipp Hackert. Ideal Landscape with Juno Temple of Agrigento. Image credit: Jacob Philipp Hackert. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Ruins, water, trees and small figures have been brought into an ordered prospect. The word “ideal” in the title is useful: the painting need not be treated as an unedited view from a single spot. Hackert connects architecture and terrain through arranged passages into the distance. The result invites movement through a composed landscape rather than a topographical checklist.

works.title: Judith with the Head of Holofernes
works.catalogueTitle: Judith with the Head of Holophernes
works.credit: Hans Baldung Grien. Judith with the Head of Holophernes. Image credit: Hans Baldung Grien. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Judith's upright, sharply outlined body appears composed beside the sword and severed head. Baldung places the violent result within a presentation that does not resemble the action of killing. The contrast complicates a simple heroic pose. Narrative knowledge and the still figure must be held together; neither alone accounts for the uneasy relation between body and attributes.

works.title: Madonna and Child with Parrots
works.credit: Hans Baldung Grien. Madonna with Child and Parrots. Image credit: Hans Baldung Grien. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The twisting child prevents the devotional pair from becoming a fixed, balanced emblem. Parrots add further points of activity near the figures, while dark drapery makes the pale bodies distinct. Baldung introduces movement into a familiar close grouping. The birds can first be noticed as compositional interruptions without assigning them an unsupported symbolic meaning.

works.title: Nativity of Christ
works.credit: Wilhelm Stetter. Nativity of Christ. Image credit: Wilhelm Stetter; Source credit: Objektkatalog der Sammlungen des Germanischen Nationalmuseums. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The Nativity occupies a setting with more than one centre of activity. Stetter's buildings divide the picture into connected spaces, permitting distant figures and surrounding worshippers to coexist with the newborn child. The eye can leave the central group and return through architectural passages. The sacred event belongs to a larger inhabited world rather than filling the image alone.

works.title: The Elder Sister
works.credit: Fritz von Uhde. The Elder Sister. Image credit: Fritz von Uhde. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Care has a weight here. The older girl carries the smaller child on her back, and Uhde makes that practical task the basis of their relation. Side light distinguishes faces and worn clothing within the modest room. The scene does not need an extraordinary event to be consequential; responsibility is already visible in the load one child bears.

closingSections.title: From heroic effort to ordinary work
paragraphs: Return from the elder sister to Hercules and compare how each body carries force. The subjects differ greatly, but both depend on a legible pose. Some collection works are loans, and holdings do not guarantee display; check the museum's current information for individual objects.
